# trafficserver / fuzz_json

trafficserver's own fuzz target `fuzz_json` ([source](source/fuzz_json.cc), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over trafficserver (apache/trafficserver at 97d2831f).

Copies the input (size_data from 5 to 1024 bytes) into a string and passes it as a JSON-RPC 2.0 message to rpc::JsonRPCManager::handle_call, with a default-constructed rpc::Context, on a new manager to which the harness adds no handlers (only the manager's own show_registered_handlers and get_service_descriptor methods are registered), and drops the response. Before the call it installs a new Diags object with DiagsPtr::set, and it deletes that object after. It returns -1 for an input with size_data below 5 or above 1024.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against trafficserver at commit 97d2831f with 3 patches to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/fuzz_json.cc is trafficserver 97d2831f's tests/fuzzing/fuzz_json.cc with one Theorem Labs change: its length check returns -1, not 1, for an input outside its limits (libFuzzer rejects the input; the driver exits 0, not 78).

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends.
